name: The Magnetic Fields
label: Merge
lede: A studio project from Boston that wrote sixty-nine love songs in a bar, fifty songs about its own life, and never once turned the volume up for its singer's ears.

eras.title: Buffalo Rome, billed as Magnetophone
eras.text: Stephin Merritt started the Magnetic Fields in Boston as a studio project with a borrowed voice: Susan Anway sang, Merritt wrote and played nearly everything. Claudia Gonson, his friend since high school, drummed and soon ran the business.

years.h: Stephin Merritt's studio project Buffalo Rome becomes a band
years.p: In Boston, Stephin Merritt's home-recording project, first called Buffalo Rome, turns into the Magnetic Fields, with Claudia Gonson, cellist [[Sam Davol|c006431f-477c-4284-af67-41adf9a062d1]] and singer Susan Anway.
years.xp: Merritt and Gonson had played together as teenagers in a band called the Zinnias. Gonson has said the early lineup was deliberately one lesbian, one gay man, one straight woman and one straight man.

years.h: First Magnetic Fields show, at T.T. the Bear's, billed wrong
years.p: The Magnetic Fields' live debut at T.T. the Bear's Place in Cambridge, Massachusetts, goes up on the listings as Magnetophone.

years.h: Distant Plastic Trees, with Susan Anway singing
years.p: The debut album pairs Stephin Merritt's cheap synths with Susan Anway's voice. Its single, 100,000 Fireflies, becomes an early cult favorite.

years.h: The Wayward Bus: Susan Anway's last Magnetic Fields album
years.p: The second album is the last with Susan Anway out front. From the House of Tomorrow EP on, Stephin Merritt sings the songs himself in his low baritone.

eras.title: Highways, holidays and side projects
eras.text: Now fronted by Stephin Merritt's own voice, the band put out two albums in a year and landed on Merge. Merritt also started spinning off other bands to hold all the songs, a habit he never broke.

years.h: Holiday on Feel Good All Over
years.p: The Magnetic Fields' third album comes out on the small Feel Good All Over label, synth-pop with Stephin Merritt now singing lead.

years.h: The Charm of the Highway Strip, first Magnetic Fields on Merge
years.p: Stephin Merritt's road-and-rails concept record, country songs played on synthesizers, is the band's first album for Merge.

years.h: Guitarist [[John Woo|00c1e96b-5294-4e93-b9f1-ec6667aff395]] joins the Magnetic Fields
years.p: John Woo comes in on guitar and banjo. He's still in the band three decades later.

years.h: Get Lost closes out the synth-pop years
years.p: The Magnetic Fields' fifth album, on Merge. Stephin Merritt is already writing for [[The 6ths|f65498b7-5c06-4bb5-801d-885595fc8bcc]], his project with guest singers, and soon for [[Future Bible Heroes|16f13f40-b8f8-42c5-a52a-cf3763002095]] with Claudia Gonson on vocals.

eras.title: Sixty-nine songs at Dick's Bar
eras.text: One idea in a Manhattan piano bar turned into a three-disc album that critics ranked with the year's biggest records. 69 Love Songs made Stephin Merritt a songwriter other songwriters quote.

years.h: Stephin Merritt plans 100 love songs in a piano bar
years.p: Listening to a pianist play Stephen Sondheim in a gay piano bar in Manhattan, Stephin Merritt decides to write 100 love songs as a stage revue. He settles on 69.
years.xp:
The revue was to star four drag queens, with the audience voting on who got paid. Merritt read about Charles Ives's 114 Songs the same day and took it as proof a giant song collection could work.

He wrote much of the album at Dick's Bar in New York, sitting there about eight hours a day.

years.h: Four studios, five singers, about a hundred instruments
years.p: Stephin Merritt records 69 Love Songs across Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics, handing some lead vocals to Claudia Gonson, [[LD Beghtol|285c8dc2-44bd-40f5-8d5b-d67f6985ed33]], Dudley Klute and [[Shirley Simms|1f0ba7b7-57b5-4d0a-ba8b-3d0ea4803ce3]].
years.xp: Sam Davol plays cello and flute, John Woo banjo, lead guitar and mandolin. [[Daniel Handler|283a74d8-ba3f-4710-8e59-22eb7caad238]], later Lemony Snicket, plays accordion and interviews Merritt for the booklet.

years.h: 69 Love Songs · three discs on Merge
years.p: 172 minutes across three volumes, sold as a box and separately. It finishes second in the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll, behind [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]]'s Play, and Robert Christgau names it his album of the year.
years.xp: Spin gave it 10 out of 10. By 2015, Nielsen counted 83,000 boxed sets sold, plus 58,000, 34,000 and 29,000 copies of the three single volumes.

q: 69 Love Songs is not remotely an album about love.
years.h: Stephin Merritt: 69 Love Songs isn't about love
years.p: Stephin Merritt insists the album is about the form, not the feeling: straight, gay and bisexual love songs in country, synth-pop, free jazz and show-tune clothes.

years.h: The Magnetic Fields play all 69 songs over two nights
years.p: The band starts performing 69 Love Songs in order across two nights, seven times in all: five in the United States and twice in London.

eras.title: The no-synth trilogy
eras.text: On Nonesuch, Stephin Merritt set himself rules: no synthesizers for three albums, one album where every title starts with I. He also wrote for the stage, for Lemony Snicket and for a documentary crew that followed him for ten years.

years.h: i: every song title starts with the letter I
years.p: The first Magnetic Fields album on Nonesuch and the first of three with no synthesizers at all.

years.h: [[Shirley Simms|1f0ba7b7-57b5-4d0a-ba8b-3d0ea4803ce3]] joins the Magnetic Fields full-time
years.p: Shirley Simms, one of the voices on 69 Love Songs, becomes a full member on autoharp, ukulele and vocals.

years.h: Distortion: pop songs buried in feedback
years.p: Still no synths, but guitars and noise instead, in the manner of [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. The band plays mini-residencies at Chicago's Old Town School of Folk Music.
years.xp: A loud record from a man with hyperacusis, painful sensitivity to sound that Stephin Merritt traces to an [[Einstürzende Neubauten|6e9ac29b-798c-4af7-8d9e-55cdc72a999c]] show at New York's Danceteria. Magnetic Fields shows stay hushed, and Merritt has been known to cover an ear during applause.

years.h: Stephin Merritt writes the Coraline musical
years.p: Stephin Merritt writes music and lyrics for the Off-Broadway adaptation of Neil Gaiman's Coraline. He'd already recorded songs for the Lemony Snicket audiobooks as [[The Gothic Archies|8008b8a9-858b-4df2-b645-6d7983556485]].

years.h: Realism ends the no-synth trilogy with folk
years.p: Acoustic instruments only, the folk mirror image of Distortion, on Nonesuch.

years.cap: Strange Powers, dir. Kerthy Fix and Gail O'Hara.
years.h: Strange Powers, a documentary ten years in the making
years.p: Kerthy Fix and Gail O'Hara's film on Stephin Merritt and the Magnetic Fields premieres after a decade of shooting. It wins Outfest's 2010 Grand Jury Prize for documentary.

eras.title: Synths back, fifty years sung
eras.text: The Magnetic Fields went back to Merge and back to synthesizers, played a festival curated by Jeff Mangum, then Stephin Merritt turned to the biggest subject he'd avoided: himself.

years.h: The Magnetic Fields play Jeff Mangum's ATP in Minehead
years.p: The band plays the All Tomorrow's Parties weekend in Minehead, England, curated by [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]].

years.h: Love at the Bottom of the Sea brings the synths back
years.p: Back on Merge, fifteen short songs full of new synthesizer tricks. The single Andrew in Drag gets played on CBS News and NPR's All Songs Considered.
play: Love at the Bottom of the Sea

years.h: Stephin Merritt meets his biological father, Scott Fagan
years.p: Stephin Merritt meets the singer-songwriter Scott Fagan, his biological father, at a film screening.

years.h: [[Chris Ewen|3b9666db-70b8-4693-9ac9-283d8af8f384]] and Anthony Kaczynski join the Magnetic Fields
years.p: Synth player Chris Ewen, an engineer and arranger on 69 Love Songs, and guitarist Anthony Kaczynski become members.

years.h: 50 Song Memoir: one song for each year of Stephin Merritt's life
years.p: For his 50th birthday, Stephin Merritt writes a song for each year since he was born, on Nonesuch.

eras.title: Quick songs, an old voice gone
eras.text: In lockdown the Magnetic Fields released a box of tiny songs. The next year the band lost Susan Anway, the voice on its first two records.

years.h: Quickies: 28 songs, none past three minutes
years.p: Nonesuch releases it digitally first, then as a box of vinyl singles on May 29 and a CD in June. Singles include Kraftwerk in a Blackout and I Want to Join a Biker Gang.

years.h: Susan Anway, the Magnetic Fields' first singer, dies
years.p: Susan Anway, who sang on Distant Plastic Trees and The Wayward Bus, dies in September 2021.
